newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cardoso orders probe into alleged Brazil navy scam.
newsitem.headline: Cardoso orders probe into alleged Brazil navy scam.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso ordered the navy on Tuesday to investigate an allegation that warships were being used to smuggle contraband into the country, an official said.
"The president requested an investigation to establish whether what happened was within or outside the rules," presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral told reporters.

Globo television, which claimed on Monday that the navy was involved in smuggling, on Tuesday broadcast footage of dozens of boxes of electronic equipment being loaded onto an aircraft carrier in San Juan, Puerto Rico last year.
Globo also showed the boxes being placed on helicopters when the boat was close to the coast of Rio de Janeiro state. The television station said the goods were then flown to a naval base near Rio.
Senior naval officers, who met with Cardoso, denied the allegations and said they would allow tax officials to inspect vessels which are not normally visted by customs staff.

"It will be the Federal Tax Secretariat that decides whether our crews are bringing in goods over and above their individual limits," navy secretary-general Carlos Eduardo Lacerda said after meeting with tax officials.
Lacerda said any sailors found with undeclared goods in excess of a $500 tax-free limit were automatically punished by the navy.

Globo claimed the scam was run by a former navy officer and a businessman in Miami who sent items -- including television sets, fax machines and perfume -- from the United States to Brazilian navy vessels in foreign ports.
